meta.granularity_note: Evidence artifacts are section-granular: a registered test file or suite exercises the requirement sections behavior collectively, not each requirement individually. A requirement with pass on all required kinds is verified at section granularity; per-requirement proof obligations remain for gate review (56.01).

V3-01.01.title: Verbatim supplies bounded, inspectable, authorized memory to agents; it is not an autonomous assistant, an answer model, or a substitute for host policy.

V3-01.02.title: The primary users are individual agent owners, developers embedding memory, teams operating shared workspaces, operators of multi-agent fleets, and hosts that expose memory to many agent products.

V3-01.03.title: The primary workloads are changing personal/project facts, cross-session investigations, coding and computer-use agents that repeat related tasks, task handoffs between agents, and long-running services that must not act on stale state.

V3-01.04.title: The product promise is inspectable, governed learning: what was recorded, how it was interpreted, what was learned from it, why it was selected, how it influenced an action, and how to correct, restrict, or remove it.

V3-01.05.title: The engine maintains two planes: an evidence plane of exact supplied/observed content with provenance, and a learning plane of derived memory whose every object carries dependency edges into the evidence plane (§06, §17).

V3-01.06.title: The engine MUST NOT generate, paraphrase, or repair bytes and label them original evidence. Supplied agent/model output may be recorded exactly as evidence of that submission, with generated provenance, never as authenticated human testimony. Learning-plane model use follows §42; approved v3.0 producers remain extractive/typed/template-based, and any future generative derivative producer needs separate opt-in approval.

V3-01.07.title: Memory kinds are fact, episode, transition, procedure, observation, profile, plan, working, social, and environment; each has a declared producer, applicability rule, retention class, and deletion closure (§17).

V3-01.08.title: "Every agent" means three supported integration depths: zero-code MCP tools, a light capture SDK/event stream with prefetch hooks, and native host adapters; all three use one engine and one authorization model (§13).

V3-01.09.title: Success is measured jointly through answer support, downstream task success, negative-transfer rate, false-update rate, unauthorized disclosure rate, deletion compliance, review burden, latency, tokens, and monetary/energy cost.

V3-01.10.title: The competitive objective is a better measured quality/safety/resource frontier on declared workloads; a universal "best memory" claim is prohibited without §54 gates.

V3-01.11.title: A release publishes its tested deployment profile; embedded rules-only results cannot be substituted for semantic or service-profile results or vice versa.

V3-01.12.title: Every advertised capability needs an executable acceptance path, a failure behavior, an owner, a resource cost, and a deletion story.

V3-01.13.title: The offline core remains useful without a cloud account, GPU, daemon, vector server, or generative model; richer profiles add capability without removing the core's guarantees.

V3-01.14.title: The host's model remains responsible for reasoning and acting; memory fidelity, procedure quality, and controller routing never guarantee a correct final action.

V3-01.15.title: More stored memory, more retrieved context, or more frequent reuse MUST NOT be presented as intrinsic quality; the engine measures and reports when memory hurt.

V3-01.16.title: No-downside marketing is prohibited: optionality, measured trade-offs, safe fallbacks, quarantine, and reversibility are the actual product mechanisms.

V3-02.01.title: Each commitment above maps to at least one requirement, one test family (§56), and one evaluation slice (§53); a commitment without measured effect is removed from the recommended profile. Broader survey context for these findings is recorded in S100–S103.

V3-02.02.title: Documented competitor capabilities are inputs to experiments; a copied headline score never satisfies a Verbatim gate.

V3-02.03.title: Research methods adopted from papers are re-evaluated on Verbatim workloads with the paper's own controls before becoming defaults.

V3-02.04.title: Findings that contradict each other (for example finer memory granularity helping and hurting) are resolved by declared ablations, not by preference.

V3-02.05.title: Every source in §61 records an observation date; mutable documentation is never cited as a permanent guarantee of a competitor's behavior.

V3-02.06.title: Hosted editions, open-source editions, research prototypes, and historical plugin versions are identified separately in every comparison; a hosted-only capability is not attributed to an OSS edition.

V3-02.07.title: Local-first storage, temporal metadata, citations, graphs, file projections, and multiple adapters are not claimed as unique inventions; differentiation claims name the measured axis.

V3-02.08.title: The competitive hypotheses are H1 fewer unsupported memory mutations at comparable useful recall, H2 higher answer-support density per token with contradiction closure, H3 task improvement from environment-qualified experience without negative transfer, H4 lower disclosure and leakage at equal utility in shared settings, and H5 lower operational complexity at a declared scale; each maps to a §54 gate.

V3-03.06.title: Corrections that change public behavior (abstention, admission, scope helpers) ship with migration notes and dry-run impact counts.

V3-04.01.title: V2-04.01 through V2-04.18 remain in force for the SQLite v3.0 profiles: exact accepted-view quotations, selected/typed interpretations, eligibility before truncation and final delivery, authenticated caller independence, separate readiness states, durable receipts, idempotent effects, lease fencing, atomic index effects, distinct temporal semantics, no future leakage, current suppression precedence, no model-granted authority, no collapsed truth score, offline modes without network, and stable host prompts. A future reviewed server engine replaces only the SQLite-specific authority binding, never the evidence/event authority or safety invariants (§62).

V3-04.02.title: Every learning-plane object MUST carry dependency edges to exact evidence revisions and to the interpretation, model, rubric, or policy revision that produced it.

V3-04.03.title: A derived object (observation, profile, procedure, transition, plan) MUST NOT be rendered as a quotation, attributed to a speaker as testimony, or count as independent corroboration of its own sources.

V3-04.04.title: A procedure, playbook, or recalled instruction confers no permission; the host checks tool permissions at execution time and treats retrieved instructions as untrusted data.

V3-04.05.title: The memory controller and any learned policy MUST NOT widen authorization, skip eligibility, bypass suppression, exceed budgets, or alter truth; they only choose among already-authorized routes.

V3-04.06.title: Detected or owner-declared sensitive values MUST NOT enter ordinary embeddings, lexical indexes, logs, telemetry, exports, or unauthorized context; controlled hydration requires task need, recipient binding, and consent (§35). Detector false negatives are separately measured and never described as impossible.

V3-04.07.title: Promotion of content into durable semantic or procedural memory requires trust and taint checks; quarantined content cannot influence retrieval, consolidation, or procedures until reviewed.

V3-04.08.title: Deletion closure covers evidence, derivations, vectors, indexes, vault entries, projections, replay snapshots, and recorded disclosures; it reports what cannot be revoked.

V3-04.09.title: A fact records who asserted it, whom it is about, who observed it, and for whom it is visible; these roles are never conflated or inferred silently.

V3-04.10.title: Stale state is candidate context, not authority; consequential actions require freshness classes or re-validation signals in the delivered context (§24).

V3-04.11.title: Every retrieval/controller receipt records policy, epochs, budgets, input references, and replay capability. Exact decision replay requires consent-retained inputs and recorded lane results/deadline cutoffs; digests alone cannot reconstruct a query and re-inference is not guaranteed identical. Erasure or expired input retention makes replay `unavailable`, never resurrects content. Metadata-only auditing remains useful without creating a hidden query-text store.

V3-04.12.title: Every learned or model-assisted component has a deterministic fallback that satisfies the same authorization and privacy contract.

V3-04.13.title: Cross-agent propagation of memory is recorded with recipient, permission, epoch, and purpose so blast radius can be computed and revoked.

V3-04.14.title: Host system prompts and tool schemas remain byte-stable within a session; memory arrives only through approved data channels.

V3-04.15.title: No telemetry, crash upload, registry check, or artifact download occurs without explicit opt-in; the default package attempts no network.

V3-04.16.title: An optional capability that fails may reduce quality but MUST NOT silently reduce authorization, privacy, durability, or deletion guarantees.

V3-05.01.title: Capability metadata distinguishes implemented, installed, configured, authorized, healthy, measured, and recommended; `status` reports all seven.

V3-05.02.title: A profile is a validated bundle of configuration and dependency requirements; selecting one MUST NOT enable capture, sharing, inference, learning, or supersession implicitly.

V3-05.03.title: Every profile passes the same authorization, privacy, deletion, and evidence suites; profiles differ in scale and inference, never in safety.

V3-05.04.title: `scaled_service` is advertised only for corpus/resource configurations that passed the §44 mixed-load matrix on the reviewed engine.

V3-05.05.title: `split_privacy` never sends vault values, raw sources, or unsanitized spans to enrichment processors or cloud models. Separately consented broker-to-task-tool disclosures follow §35 rather than enrichment consent; every recipient is enumerated and audited.

V3-05.06.title: Deferred capabilities remain visible in the release manifest and cannot appear as completed checklist items.

V3-05.07.title: An optional capability is not a v3.0 blocker when absent and honestly reported unavailable; if shipped or advertised, all its required enabled, denied, degraded, and recovery cases become mandatory.

V3-05.08.title: Before implementation, freeze a release manifest mapping each requirement and scenario to capability, tier, profile, required evidence, and owner. Core items cannot become `not_applicable` by disabling them. Optional/research omissions are recorded as deferred, not passed.

V3-05.09.title: In mixed sections, shared evidence/security invariants bind every shipped capability; capability-specific paragraphs about observations (§23), social memory (§25), remote protocols (§48), projections (§50), workbench (§52), learned policies (§26/§43), and non-SQLite engines (§38) bind only their manifest entries. §55 defines scenario applicability and §63 uses that same manifest.

V3-05.10.title: The first release proves cross-host reuse in one authority domain. This does not require A2A, cross-device replication, or a server engine; Hermes and ADK use the same capture and evidence contracts against isolated, owner-approved test stores.

V3-06.01.title: `api.py` becomes a facade plus topic siblings (`api_ingest.py`, `api_recall.py`, `api_review.py`, `api_governance.py`, `api_privacy.py`, `api_experience.py`); siblings own one topic each and import the facade only lazily.

V3-06.02.title: Shared helpers (`has_table`, `ensure_scope`, digest utilities, JSON safety) exist once in `storage/` or `core/`; duplicate definitions fail a lint gate.

V3-06.03.title: `hrr.py` is removed from the shipped package unless a §53 ablation demonstrates benefit; research code lives under `research/` outside the distribution.

V3-06.04.title: Engine construction receives host context, governance service, clock, configuration, capability factories, and controller policy explicitly; nothing is discovered from process state.

V3-06.05.title: Evidence-plane writes are append-only except for authorized suppression and purge; learning-plane objects are revisioned and invalidated by dependency changes.

V3-06.06.title: A materialized dependency graph (`derivations`) connects every learning-plane object to its evidence and producer revisions; purge, invalidation, and influence tracing traverse it.

V3-06.07.title: Policy and controller code compute typed plans from immutable snapshots; effect services validate and apply them inside one transaction with expected versions.

V3-06.08.title: Model calls, artifact loading, connector I/O, and remote processing occur outside write transactions and outside unbounded read snapshots.

V3-06.09.title: Importing any package MUST NOT create stores, download artifacts, start threads, select profiles, bind sockets, or dispatch requests.

V3-06.10.title: Adapters translate only; admission, authorization, screening, and storage logic never exist in an adapter.

V3-06.11.title: Production paths MUST NOT fall back to duplicate SQL after arbitrary repository exceptions; classified failures fail closed or degrade explicitly.

V3-06.12.title: Every cross-package contract (envelope, receipt, request, bundle, capsule, event) has a versioned schema and consumer tests in the same change.

V3-07.01.title: Precedence is defaults, profile, configuration file, then explicit invocation overrides; environment variables are secrets references only.

V3-07.02.title: Validation resolves deferred annotations, rejects string booleans, bool-as-int, non-finite numbers, duplicate keys, unknown fields, and incompatible mode/profile/lane/backend combinations before any side effect.

V3-07.03.title: Mode or profile changes increment the policy epoch, cancel disallowed queued work, and prevent stale in-flight results from gaining new authority.

V3-07.04.title: Learned controller policies, observation injection, automatic promotion, and balanced admission each require a recorded gate artifact identifier in configuration; absence keeps the deterministic behavior.

V3-07.05.title: Security tightening applies immediately; prompt/tool-affecting changes take effect in the next session unless the host supports explicit immediate application.

V3-07.06.title: Runtime status describes effective capabilities, not requested ones; a requested lane without a healthy index is reported unavailable.

V3-07.07.title: Configuration changes record old/new digests and field names; private values are never copied into audit events or exports.

V3-07.08.title: A v2 configuration opens read-only until migrated; migration never enables capture, sharing, inference, learning, or supersession.

V3-08.01.title: Every call binds an authenticated principal outside request parameters; claimed actor names, source text, and model output never establish identity.

V3-08.02.title: An agent principal is distinct from the human it serves; delegated authority is recorded as a delegation edge with expiry, not as identity substitution.

V3-08.03.title: Each evidence item records asserter, subject(s), observer, and audience; each learning-plane object inherits and may narrow these roles but never widens them.

V3-08.04.title: Perspective-scoped memory is supported: what agent A observed about B, what B asserted about itself, and what a workspace has published are distinct records with distinct visibility.

V3-08.05.title: Per-turn author identity is read for every turn in shared sessions; caching the first participant as every later speaker is a defect.

V3-08.06.title: Reported speech records reporter and attributed speaker separately and does not inherit direct-principal authority.

V3-08.07.title: Audiences are explicit sets; group sessions intersect the audiences of every participant before delivery, and owner-only evidence never enters a wider audience.

V3-08.08.title: Service profiles MAY verify workload identity through SPIFFE SVIDs or OAuth client identity [S80, S74]; embedded profiles bind identity through the launching host.

V3-08.09.title: Identity mappings across hosts (the same human on two agents) are explicit operator records, never inferred from display names or email-like strings.

V3-08.10.title: Principal deletion or departure triggers a governance review of owned grants, delegated authority, and shared derivations rather than silent orphaning.

V3-09.01.title: Authorization decisions are deterministic evaluations over relationship tuples (principal, relation, object) and explicit policies with forbid precedence; a request is denied unless a permit applies and no forbid applies [S82, S83].

V3-09.02.title: The embedded profile evaluates policies in-process without an external authorization service; service profiles MAY adapt to external relationship stores through an adapter that caches decisions with epochs and fails closed when unavailable.

V3-09.03.title: Grants carry scope, verbs, purposes, expiry, issuer, delegation depth, and attenuation caveats; delegation may only attenuate, never widen.

V3-09.04.title: Every scope has `authz_revision`; bound callers pin an epoch, revocation increments it, and pinned callers fence indistinguishably from missing data (v2 A17 remains).

V3-09.05.title: Revoked verbs are removed from the effective context before any dereference, including operator wildcards; re-granting is an explicit recorded event.

V3-09.06.title: Optional portable capsules carry issuer-authenticated grants with recipient, verbs, expiry, purpose, delegation chain, unique capsule id, and source-policy epoch [S84, S85]. Offline verification proves authenticity and expiry against a trusted clock, not current nonrevocation. Online use reauthorizes against the issuer; offline read/quote requires an explicit cached-authorization lease (default maximum 300 seconds, capped by grant expiry), reports `revocation_status=unknown`, and fails closed after that lease. Offline capsules never authorize `act`, `hydrate`, further delegation, or promotion. Local import permission is still required; foreign grants never become local authority automatically. GNAP/OAuth is an optional transport for the same attenuated grants [S104].

V3-09.07.title: `act` is never implied by `read` or `quote`. The engine controls ticket issuance; enforcement exists only at registered gateways that validate the current grant, epochs, purpose, exact action digest, recipient, expiry, and one-use nonce immediately before execution and independently apply host tool policy. Default ticket lifetime is 30 seconds with a maximum of 60 seconds. Without such a gateway, `action_use_enforcement=advisory_only`; Verbatim cannot prevent a model from acting on already delivered text and MUST NOT advertise that it can.

V3-09.08.title: Purpose limitation binds grants and requests; a request declaring purpose `debugging` cannot receive evidence granted only for purpose `personal_assistance`.

V3-09.09.title: Authorization precedes dereference of private identifiers; unauthorized and nonexistent objects produce the same public error class.

V3-09.10.title: Administrative verbs cannot be exercised through model-visible tools; MCP and framework adapters expose no `admin` surface.

V3-09.11.title: Grant changes, delegations, revocations, and denials are audited with safe identifiers; audit rows never contain evidence text.

V3-09.12.title: Authorization state exports with bundles as data, never as automatically effective authority in the destination.

V3-09.13.title: Tests exercise forged scopes, actor names, audience widening through group sessions, delegation depth overflow, expired capsules, and revocation races against warm caches. Optional gateway tests include mismatched actions, nonce replay, expired tickets, and grant revocation between retrieval and execution.

V3-09.14.title: Derived visibility is the intersection of all contributing parents' permitted audiences, purposes, and retention constraints, evaluated under current authorization. `derive` does not confer `read`, `quote`, or declassification. A summary cannot disclose information from a parent its recipient is denied; `quote` controls verbatim access, not a promise that readable summaries hide the underlying facts.

V3-09.15.title: Admission, derived publication, ticket/value release, and final bundle delivery recheck authorization, suppression, and input revisions at a documented linearization point. Revocation/suppression immediately fences affected descendants; asynchronous recomputation never leaves an old derived object readable while waiting for cleanup. Once bytes have been delivered they cannot be recalled.

V3-10.01.title: Agent-authored memory is labeled `agent_generated` with the producing agent, model identity where known, and task; it never becomes human testimony.

V3-10.02.title: A later write by another agent cannot overwrite a human-owned fact; it creates a perspective-scoped claim or opens a conflict group for review.

V3-10.03.title: Handoff capsules bind recipient, verbs, expiry, purpose, evidence dependencies, security metadata, and freshness classes; recipients cannot widen them.

V3-10.04.title: Every propagation (share, handoff, publication, hydration) is recorded in a propagation ledger with epoch and purpose so blast radius is computable per source revision.

V3-10.05.title: Fleet revocation marks propagated copies revoked in the ledger and notifies reachable recipients; the product states plainly that already-delivered context cannot be recalled.

V3-10.06.title: Taint and trust labels travel with propagated content; a recipient engine MUST NOT upgrade trust because the sender is an agent.

V3-10.07.title: Contradictions between agents persist as unresolved groups with perspective attribution; recency, popularity, or orchestrator rank never declares truth.

V3-10.08.title: Shared-memory quality is reported as utility, unauthorized-disclosure rate, and deletion-compliance failure rate together, following governance benchmark practice [S60, S61]; a high utility score cannot hide leakage.

V3-10.09.title: Orchestrators receive typed conflict, staleness, and quarantine reports; delegating a task never grants the delegate the orchestrator's memory verbs.

V3-10.10.title: Social memory about collaborators (communication preferences, reliability of past outputs) is a derived learning-plane object about an agent, visible only within the observing principal's scope unless published (§25).

V3-10.11.title: The A2A adapter exposes handoff capsules as an extension with explicit capability negotiation; A2A tasks never carry raw scopes or grants [S72].

V3-10.12.title: Tests include two-agent leak attempts through shared sessions, delegation replays after revocation, and deletion requests observed by a second agent.

V3-11.01.title: Consent records identify processor, purpose, data classes, sanitization level, retention promise, budget, and expiry; a grant of memory access is not consent to disclose to a processor.

V3-11.02.title: Enrichment egress classes are `none`, `sanitized`, `evidence_excerpt`, and `full`; no class permits vault values. Downstream value use is a separate disclosure channel (§35) with an authenticated recipient and purpose; consent for enrichment never permits hydration. `split_privacy` prohibits vault values in any cloud-model context, while a separately consented task tool may receive only its required value through a brokered handle. Sanitization reduces exposure but does not establish anonymity: surrounding text and stable placeholders can identify people.

V3-11.03.title: Every remote call records purpose, processor, byte counts, data class, epoch, and outcome as an egress receipt; receipts are inspectable and purge-aware.

V3-11.04.title: Budgets are reserved before dispatch and released on completion; timeouts keep conservative reservations.

V3-11.05.title: Where a host supports MCP elicitation, consent MAY be requested through form mode with a structured schema [S73]; the engine never blocks core operations awaiting elicitation and never assumes consent from silence.

V3-11.06.title: Purpose strings come from a registry; free-text purposes are rejected so that limitation is enforceable.

V3-11.07.title: Hydration of vault values requires a consent record whose purpose matches the request and whose expiry has not passed; each hydration is a disclosure event.

V3-11.08.title: Consent withdrawal stops future disclosure immediately, cancels queued remote work for that processor, and marks outstanding results stale.

V3-11.09.title: Telemetry and crash reporting are separate opt-ins with metadata-only payloads and documented fields.

V3-11.10.title: Zero daily budget disables remote inference including nominally free services; no product text promises permanent free inference.

V3-11.11.title: Tool execution permission, retention consent, derivation permission, and disclosure consent are independent decisions. An approved file read, browser action, or ACP `allow_once` result is not retention consent. Capture authorization records allowed source classes, scopes, retention policy, issuer, policy revision, and expiry; only host/operator surfaces issue it.

V3-11.12.title: A caller's purpose declaration is checked against its preauthorized registry entries; it does not prove actual downstream intent. Hosts disclose which enforcement they provide, including whether retrieved or hydrated bytes enter a local model, a named cloud model, or a task tool. Unknown downstream processing denies value hydration rather than guessing locality.

V3-12.01.title: `SourceEnvelopeV3` includes kind, host/session/task/step identifiers, actor principal, perspective roles, event time, receipt time, content bytes or artifact reference, media type, size, trust class, capture-permission proof, redaction status, and adapter version.

V3-12.02.title: A trajectory is an ordered set of steps within a task; each step references its action envelope, observation envelope(s), state-delta references, and the environment fingerprint current at that step.

V3-12.03.title: Outcome envelopes record success, failure, partial, or unknown from an identified checker; an agent's statement of completion is never an outcome.

V3-12.04.title: Ingestion is idempotent by host identifiers or documented sequence keys; retries and final-session capture produce one logical source.

V3-12.05.title: Streams accept JSONL envelopes with backpressure and bounded in-flight counts; acceptance receipts separate durable acceptance from interpretation readiness.

V3-12.06.title: Large artifacts are stored as content-addressed blobs with per-kind size limits and are referenced by envelopes; exceeding limits stores metadata plus a truncation record, never a silently cut artifact presented as complete.

V3-12.07.title: Pre-persistence scrubbing removes detected/declared credentials and policy-prohibited arguments before durable bytes are written, including blob artifacts; unsafe-to-scrub source kinds fail closed. Record non-content redaction spans and accepted-view offsets so quotations remain honest; detection coverage and misses follow §35.

V3-12.08.title: Byte fidelity applies to accepted content; extracted text views (diff hunks, HTML text, transcript text) are separate revisions with locators, and quotations cite the view.

V3-12.09.title: Cron, flush, and subagent contexts skip automatic capture by default; parent-side delegation observations retain generated/observed provenance.

V3-12.10.title: Envelopes without capture permission proof for a gated kind are rejected with a typed error, not silently downgraded to another kind.

V3-12.11.title: Time fields distinguish event time supplied by the host from receipt time assigned by the engine; neither is trusted for validity intervals without interpretation.

V3-12.12.title: Capture per principal MAY follow a `per_principal` worth-storing policy only after G2 measurement [S48, S49]; the default is uniform conservative capture.

V3-13.01.title: All depths use one engine, one authorization model, and one receipt contract; an adapter cannot obtain capabilities the engine would deny a direct caller.

V3-13.02.title: The capture SDK defines a language-neutral JSONL/HTTP event schema with Python and TypeScript reference implementations; conformance is tested through a published kit.

V3-13.03.title: Hosts own authentication, per-turn author identity, capture permission, tool permission, and prompt assembly; the engine owns storage, interpretation, authorization enforcement, retrieval, and deletion.

V3-13.04.title: `on_compaction` lets a host archive eligible context before summarization so exact details remain recoverable; strict checkpoint mode is advertised only when every required input is durably archived.

V3-13.05.title: `on_task_end` delivers outcome evidence with checker identity; missing outcomes are recorded as unknown, never inferred as success.

V3-13.06.title: Prefetch obeys host deadlines, returns local results or explicit degraded outcomes, and never rewrites system prompts, tool schemas, or delivered history.

V3-13.07.title: The adapter conformance kit covers restart, scope narrowing, cancellation, receipts, A→B→A profile isolation, denied callers, and revocation during a session.

V3-13.08.title: Depth-0 tools accept no profile, actor, endpoint, grant, or approval arguments; such fields are rejected, not ignored.

V3-13.09.title: Native adapters use host-supported threading and context propagation; credentials use scoped host access without environment fallthrough.

V3-13.10.title: Adapters publish a capability matrix (capture kinds, hooks, outcome delivery, compaction archive, downstream processors, gateway enforcement) so operators know which features and guarantees a host supports.

V3-13.11.title: `verbatim_capture` takes `operation_id` and either bounded UTF-8 `text` (maximum 64 KiB) or an opaque `host_source_handle`, never both. Text is recorded exactly as submitted but attributed only to the authenticated agent as `agent_note`/`agent_generated`, even if it claims to quote a user. A host handle resolves through a registered trusted adapter and carries its actual author, revision, consent, and audience; the model cannot mint its attestation. No arbitrary file path or URL is fetched.

V3-13.12.title: Explicit agent-note capture requires `ingest` plus the setup-issued `capture.explicit_agent_notes` grant; it does not enable other capture classes or bypass sensitivity/screening. The core has an evidence-only archive path for accepted nonquarantined notes so a depth-0 client can recall its own submissions without promotion. Such results say `agent-submitted; not verified user testimony` and never supersede human assertions.

V3-13.13.title: The capture receipt returns source/view revision, accepted byte length, readiness, and bounded authorized span handles. `verbatim_remember` selects an existing span handle or exact validated ranges and remains a proposal, not free-form fact insertion. B39 starts from an empty store and exercises capture → receipt/readiness → archive recall → grounded proposal → restart using only MCP, with no Python pre-seeding or claimed automatic admission.

V3-14.01.title: Security metadata has independent dimensions: `source_trust` (the provenance classes above), `content_form` (`descriptive`, `instructional`, `mixed`, `unknown`), `attack_risk` (`unassessed`, `no_findings`, `suspicious`, `blocked`), and `review_state` (`not_required`, `pending`, `released`, `quarantined`, `rejected`). They are not one ordered taint scale. `no_findings` means screening found no listed attack signal, not certified safety; origin never changes after review.

V3-14.02.title: The instruction/evidence classifier identifies content form and claimed instruction target. Imperatives in an installation guide, test recipe, or safety runbook are not attacks merely because they are instructions. Screening separately detects attempts to redirect the receiving agent's authority, disclosure, or persistence behavior; every finding references the relevant spans and rule/classifier revision.

V3-14.03.title: Retained, interpreted, admitted, promoted, and shared are distinct processing/authorization milestones, not one universal truth ladder. Evidence-only archive recall is allowed under §13; promotion to durable facts or procedures and sharing each require separate decisions.

V3-14.04.title: External instructions with no unresolved attack finding may be quoted with provenance and may contribute to a reviewed procedure with observed outcome evidence. Unknown provenance, suspicious findings, or blocked content prevent automatic promotion. Review can approve a specific use without relabeling the source `principal_direct` or removing its history.

V3-14.05.title: Phrases such as "remember to" or "always" are features, not automatic quarantine triggers. A deterministic block names the attempted boundary violation and its context; ambiguous findings stay pending review. Reviewers may append a scoped release decision for a false positive with expected versions and rationale; model confidence alone cannot clear a finding.

V3-14.06.title: Compaction-driven and experience-to-procedure writes are separately screened write channels because they can launder external instructions into durable memory [S55]. Derived metadata unions parent origins, preserves all open findings, and carries the most restrictive unresolved disposition; composition is re-screened rather than assumed safe from individually passed items.

V3-14.07.title: Anomaly signals (rapid changes to stable facts, unusual write volume, new principal writing to old scopes, oversized items) open review rather than auto-admit; they do not establish an attack by themselves.

V3-14.08.title: Sensitivity routing precedes durable writes for detected or declared vault-routed classes (§35). Detection has a measured miss rate; the enforceable invariant is that an item classified S2/S3 cannot be routed to plaintext storage and S4 cannot be retained.

V3-14.09.title: Trust class is never raised by retrieval frequency, helpfulness votes, agent confidence, or repetition across derived copies. Host-observed transport proves what the tool returned, not that external text inside its result is trustworthy.

V3-14.10.title: Quarantined content is excluded from ordinary retrieval, consolidation, procedures, sharing, and exports. Authorized reviewers see it through an isolated operator surface, not automatic agent prefetch; release, suppress, and purge remain separate actions.

V3-14.11.title: Screening reports false-positive and retained-coverage rates separately for benign chat, external documentation, installation guides, runbooks, exact commands, and safety procedures. It fails its gate if aggregate performance hides severe blocking of a useful category; B45 includes "Run pnpm test before merging" as a benign procedural instruction.

V3-15.01.title: Segmentation retains meaningful punctuation-light chat facts while excluding bounded acknowledgements; the realistic-chat regression slice guards this behavior.

V3-15.02.title: Unicode-aware signal detection covers all scripts; scripts that `unicode61` cannot segment (CJK, Thai, Khmer, Myanmar, Lao) use a bounded character n-gram or dictionary-segmented lexical projection rather than substring scans at scale.

V3-15.03.title: Language packs declare grammar coverage for negation, time, conditions, contrast, and predicates; unsupported languages keep exact evidence and lexical/semantic recall with explicit interpretation status.

V3-15.04.title: Code blocks, diffs, JSON, tables, paths, versions, and identifiers are tokenized by structure-aware rules; identifiers keep an exact index (v2 §28.15).

V3-15.05.title: Reference resolution binds pronouns and elliptical answers only within a bounded, authorized antecedent set using deterministic rules or typed selection with `unknown`/`multiple`; unresolved references stay unresolved.

V3-15.06.title: The predicate registry expands with community-reviewed structured predicates; open predicates arrive as typed proposals with fixtures, never as free-form slots invented at runtime.

V3-15.07.title: Negation is proposition-scoped; contrast preserves both clauses and their relation; conditions are typed with evaluable keys.

V3-15.08.title: Time expressions resolve through a deterministic interpreter with precision classes and recorded reference clocks; models never perform trusted date arithmetic.

V3-15.09.title: Numbers, units, versions, paths, and identifiers use deterministic parsers with raw evidence references.

V3-15.10.title: Entity candidates reference exact spans; identical display names do not merge; aliases require evidence or operator confirmation (§19).

V3-15.11.title: Speaker attribution and reported speech are preserved per span; first-person resolution binds to the source speaker.

V3-15.12.title: Harvester identity (version, language pack, rules digest) is persisted with every interpretation; replay under the same identity yields identical span identities.

V3-15.13.title: Tool-output harvesting extracts state facts (paths, versions, environment values) as `host_observed` claims with revalidation policies rather than durable personal facts.

V3-16.01.title: Core imports support UTF-8 text, Markdown, versioned JSONL, and code files with repository/revision identity; large files stream with explicit source/view/chunk lineage.

V3-16.02.title: PDFs and structured documents use a reviewed extraction plugin; quotations cite the extracted view plus page/locator, never fictional original byte offsets.

V3-16.03.title: Images, audio, and video are retained as approved artifacts linked to host-supplied captions or transcripts, which are derivative views; the engine invokes no OCR, speech, or vision service silently.

V3-16.04.title: C2PA or similar provenance manifests found in imported media are recorded as provenance hints, not as verified authenticity claims [S89].

V3-16.05.title: Connectors declare allowed roots/accounts, data classes, cursor semantics, revision identity, deletion handling, and rate/storage budgets; cursors advance only with durable receipts.

V3-16.06.title: Connectors never crawl credentials, browser stores, private directories, or unrelated histories automatically; each connector passes idempotency, permission, source-edit, source-delete, and offline-disabled tests.

V3-16.07.title: Connector content enters as `external_content` and follows §14 screening before any promotion.

V3-16.08.title: Source deletion upstream suppresses derived views and artifacts per the approved deletion policy, including cached previews.

V3-16.09.title: Multimodal semantic similarity remains research until same-scope filtering, evidence verification, and task benefit are demonstrated.

V3-16.10.title: Native multimedia understanding is not advertised when the implementation only indexes supplied text descriptions.

V3-17.01.title: Every kind declares producer, evidence basis, applicability rule, retention class, injection eligibility, and deletion closure; a kind missing any declaration cannot be enabled. The kinds follow the substrate/mechanism/subject taxonomy of current surveys while excluding parametric memory from the product [S100, S101].

V3-17.02.title: Derivation edges record parent object revisions, producer identity (harvester, compiler, model artifact, rubric, policy revision), and creation sequence; edges are immutable.

V3-17.03.title: Changing or suppressing a parent invalidates dependent derived revisions prospectively; recomputation appends new revisions with current recorded time and original source-time provenance.

V3-17.04.title: Derived objects render with an explicit `derived` label, their proof count of distinct evidence families, and links to exact evidence; they are never rendered as quotations.

V3-17.05.title: Proof counts measure independent evidence families, not copies, retrievals, or model confidence; they order derived objects among themselves and never override exact evidence.

V3-17.06.title: Injection eligibility (may this kind enter agent context automatically?) is separate from retrieval eligibility; observations and procedures require their gates before automatic injection.

V3-17.07.title: No kind auto-promotes another: a fact does not become an observation, an episode does not become a procedure, and a plan does not become a fact without a producer decision and its receipt.

V3-17.08.title: Each object carries a freshness class (§24) and merged multidimensional security metadata (§14) from its evidence; retrieval and assembly honor both without converting external origin into an ordered risk score.

V3-17.09.title: Kinds are filters on retrieval, never authorization shortcuts; requesting `procedure` cannot reach evidence the caller cannot `read`.

V3-17.10.title: Storage of derived objects is bounded per scope by policy; exceeding a bound triggers consolidation review or retention decisions, never silent eviction of evidence.

V3-18.12.title: Each transition, review, and relation write commits atomically with its index effects and derivation invalidations.

V3-19.01.title: Entities are scope-local records with kind, evidenced labels, evidenced aliases, and perspective; principals are immutable identities that entity aliasing cannot change.

V3-19.02.title: Co-occurrence and name similarity produce merge suggestions for review; automatic merges are limited to exact identifier matches declared by a language pack or registry.

V3-19.03.title: Merge and split are revisioned, reversible operations with dependent-claim previews; derived objects referencing merged entities are invalidated and recomputed.

V3-19.04.title: Reference resolution results record the antecedent set considered, the rule or typed selection used, and `unknown`/`multiple` outcomes; queries can request unresolved references explicitly.

V3-19.05.title: Profiles are deterministic snapshots over a pinned sequence and budget: admitted preferences, stable facts, open plans, unresolved conflicts, and freshness warnings with citations.

V3-19.06.title: Profiles are perspective-scoped: an agent's profile of a user contains only what that agent may read; published profiles are explicit acts with audiences.

V3-19.07.title: Profiles never infer psychological traits, protected attributes, or health/finance facts that were not explicitly stated and admitted; inference of such classes is prohibited (§35).

V3-19.08.title: Profile budgets are enforced in bytes and tokens; overflow drops lowest-priority derived material first and evidence citations last.

V3-19.09.title: Entity neighborhoods feed graph and causal lanes only after entity quality passes §53 ablations for the workload; otherwise entity data is a filter, not an expansion source.

V3-19.10.title: Entity and alias changes are audited and purge-aware; deleting a source revision removes aliases evidenced only by it.

V3-20.01.title: Episodes are produced automatically from trajectories (task identity), session segments (bounded gaps and topic shifts by deterministic rules), or explicit operator selection; every episode records its boundary rule.

V3-20.02.title: Transitions are deterministic records `(pre_state_refs, action_envelope, post_state_refs, checker_ref, environment_fingerprint)` derived from consecutive trajectory steps; no model invents transitions.

V3-20.03.title: State anchors describe observed environment state with exact references (file revisions, DOM/screen artifact digests, tool versions). They reconstruct observation/action order without replaying full trajectories [S38, S39]; they do not establish causation.

V3-20.04.title: Core edges are `precedes`, `observed_after`, and `verified_by`. An action followed by a state change creates `observed_after`, not `caused`. Optional causal hypotheses require a separately labeled method, competing explanations, and intervention/reproduction evidence; a passing test or reviewer approval alone is not a causal proof.

V3-20.05.title: Episode labels use extracted keywords, typed aggregates, or optional pooled embeddings. Tree-organized retrieval may index those aggregates [S103]. Generative narrative summaries are outside the approved v3.0 producer path and require a separately approved opt-in derivative producer.

V3-20.06.title: Membership history preserves attach/detach events; closed episodes remain queryable with their known-time context.

V3-20.07.title: Hierarchical retrieval (episode first, then exact members) becomes the recommended route only after it beats or complements flat hybrid search in a declared ablation.

V3-20.08.title: Episode and transition production runs as durable jobs with idempotent keys; replaying a trajectory yields identical episode and transition identities.

V3-20.09.title: Failed and abandoned episodes are retained as negative experience with their actual failure evidence and are excluded from procedure promotion unless explicitly used as counterexamples.

V3-20.10.title: Episode retrieval exposes causal paths as cited paths, never as new natural-language conclusions.

V3-21.01.title: A procedure is an evidence-backed record of how a task was attempted and what was observed; it is advice, never executable code, and never authority.

V3-21.02.title: Operations are abstracted to classes with parameter templates; instance-specific values become bindings that the host must re-obtain, following query-conditioned reuse findings [S44].

V3-21.03.title: Procedures store both a structured record and a deterministic human-readable rendering; the rendering is regenerated from the record and never edited independently.

V3-21.04.title: Procedural signatures (ordered operation classes plus intent) are indexed for structure-aware matching in addition to text and embeddings [S42].

V3-21.05.title: Failure modes are first-class: a procedure without contrary outcome evidence from a compatible environment is labeled `no_failure_evidence` rather than presumed safe.

V3-21.06.title: Risk class derives from hazards and host-declared action classes; high-risk procedures require review before activation and are excluded from automatic prefetch.

V3-21.07.title: Missing environment information reduces applicability confidence; it is never treated as a wildcard match.

V3-21.08.title: A procedure references its evidence family so copied summaries and original trajectories are counted once in success statistics.

V3-21.09.title: Procedures inherit parent provenance, open attack findings, and review dispositions through §14's merge rules. External instructional content is not inherently malicious; promotion requires a scoped reviewer decision plus verified task evidence, never a change of its source origin. Any unresolved blocked/quarantined dependency prevents activation.

V3-21.10.title: Procedure records participate fully in scope revocation, historical queries, export, and purge.

V3-22.01.title: Compilation runs as durable jobs over completed episodes: extract operations and bindings, align with transitions, attach outcomes, and produce a `candidate` procedure with provenance; build, index, patch, and prune are explicit life-cycle operations with receipts [S102].

V3-22.02.title: Compilation is recurrence-gated: a candidate is compiled when a task family recurs or an outcome is verified, bounding compute rather than compiling every trajectory eagerly [S51].

V3-22.03.title: Contrastive refinement compares compatible episodes to propose discriminating conditions and record failure modes [S43]. Differences are hypotheses, not validated preconditions or causal repairs. The core keeps observed operation order and does not invent missing steps; a proposed order change must be supported by another observed successful trajectory and explicit review.

V3-22.04.title: The promotion ladder is candidate → reviewed → active; v3.0 requires explicit review for activation. Automatic low-risk promotion remains research: it needs G5 task benefit plus a separately frozen promotion-precision/coverage protocol and artifact under §42. G5 alone is not evidence that a classifier can approve unseen procedures safely.

V3-22.05.title: Drift detection compares current environment fingerprints with a procedure's fingerprint; mismatch yields `ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH` or an explicitly uncertain suggestion.

V3-22.06.title: Reuse accounting records exposures, applicable attempts, adoptions, successes, failures, and unknown outcomes with denominators per environment class; no single self-reinforcing usefulness score exists.

V3-22.07.title: Negative transfer is estimated with paired executions (§53), not assigned from mere adoption/failure correlation [S41]. One verified applicability or safety violation suspends automatic recommendation and opens review; ordinary unpaired failures only trigger an investigation unless a preregistered paired regression threshold is crossed. Difficulty and environment mix are reported so hard tasks do not automatically discredit a useful procedure.

V3-22.08.title: Retired and deprecated procedures remain retrievable as history and as counterexamples; retirement never erases evidence.

V3-22.09.title: Agent-authored lessons are derivative proposals attached to procedures, visibly separated from observed transitions and outcomes.

V3-22.10.title: The engine never generates adaptation steps for a new environment; the host may propose them, and they become evidence only after observation.

V3-22.11.title: Hidden online exploration that inserts unvalidated procedures into real tasks to collect rewards is prohibited.

V3-22.12.title: Evaluation of procedures uses related tasks separated by repository/task family and chronological availability; future solution artifacts are forbidden inputs (§53).

V3-22.13.title: The compiler manifest pins operation mappings, binding types, checkers, parser versions, limits, and template digests; each candidate identity is derived from this manifest and its ordered evidence revisions. Repeated compilation is idempotent, and unsupported episodes retain their exact evidence without claiming a usable procedure.

V3-22.14.title: A patch body is instance-specific evidence, not a reusable patch for a different task. Reuse can suggest an evidenced workflow and checks, but the host authors task-specific edits; Verbatim neither executes stored commands nor generates new edits.

V3-22.15.title: Applicability evaluates typed conditions with true/false/unknown. Captured versions are observations; semver ranges or cross-repository compatibility are not inferred from string similarity. Only reviewer-approved conditions or a separate reproduced experiment can broaden the initial observed-environment envelope.

V3-22.16.title: A checker receipt binds checker version, repository revision/tree digest, invocation identity, selected tests, completion status, and exit/result data. V3-35.06.title: Reclassification to a stricter class immediately suppresses affected plaintext outputs and derived objects, then re-sanitizes projections in durable jobs. Previously disclosed bytes, pre-reclassification backups, and storage remanence are reported separately; migration does not retroactively promise zero exposure.

V3-35.07.title: For detected S4 values, persist only redacted accepted content and non-content redaction metadata, never the removed secret or an unkeyed digest of it. S2/S3 retention needs explicit policy and an unlocked vault; otherwise reject the write or retain only an explicitly allowed redacted view. Original and sanitized offsets are distinct: quotations cite the accepted view, and hydrated renderings are labeled composed disclosures rather than original contiguous quotations.

V3-35.08.title: `split_privacy` enrichment receives only minimized sanitized views, with per-disclosure placeholder aliases rather than stable cross-processor identifiers. The local mapping re-associates returned references; placeholders and surrounding text still undergo purpose/sensitivity checks because pseudonymization is not anonymity.

V3-35.09.title: Default backup includes ciphertext and wrapped entry keys but never scope/root keys or provider credentials. A recovery manifest identifies the separately held provider and key versions, and a restore drill proves access can be recovered without placing keys into the bundle. Loss of a current provider binding is `locked`; only confirmed loss of all recoverable key versions is labeled unrecoverable.

V3-35.10.title: Privacy evaluation reports response quality, unnecessary disclosure rate, detection misses, hydration denials, and cost together. Utility gains do not authorize extra recipients or unnecessary hydration.

V3-35.11.title: Key provision is a setup/host responsibility, not an import side effect. The required vault backend is installed with the v3 engine; without a configured host-secret provider or reviewed OS keyring, nonsensitive operation remains available but vault retention/hydration fails closed. Keys are never silently generated into the database directory.

V3-35.12.title: Key rotation is versioned and crash-recoverable: new writes use the new version, old values remain bound to recorded versions until rewrapped, and old keys retire only after live references and backup recovery obligations are resolved. A rotation receipt lists backups still dependent on the old key. Plaintext process memory, swap, crash dumps, the source host, and already disclosed copies are explicit limits, not erased by deleting a database row.

V3-36.01.title: The v2 purge contract remains: preview of exact dependencies, reversible suppression, irreversible purge, erasure epochs before physical cleanup, and verified absence from live retrieval, export, rebuild, and replay paths.

V3-36.02.title: Deletion closure extends to derivation edges, observations, profiles, procedures, transitions, vectors, sparse/late-interaction rows, vault entries, projections, replay snapshots, influence records, and recorded propagations.

V3-36.03.title: After logical purge, ordinary callers receive no erased object, detail handle, count, or existence-confirming error [S60]. A privileged erasure ledger may retain minimal non-content tombstones to prevent resurrection; its API is not ordinary recall. The guarantee is non-disclosure of suppressed records and their dependent artifacts, not that an independently retained source, a user's prior knowledge, or an external model cannot know the same fact.

V3-36.04.title: Purge verification checks dependency reachability and all implemented retrieval/index/export/replay paths, with adversarial probe and nearest-neighbor tests [S94]. Passing probes is evidence for the tested boundary, not proof of universal unlearning or forensic erasure; cleanup failure keeps the affected material suppressed and reopens the cleanup job.

V3-36.05.title: Propagated copies are marked revoked in the ledger and notified where reachable; the completion report lists recipient-controlled copies that cannot be remotely erased.

V3-36.06.title: Retention policies distinguish evidence, derived memory, vault entries, operational metadata, projections, exports, and replay artifacts; expiry warnings never authorize deletion by themselves.

V3-36.07.title: Restore from backup reapplies the current erasure ledger; without deletion knowledge, restored content stays quarantined.

V3-36.08.title: Purge reports logical suppression, canonical deletion, derived cleanup, vault key destruction, index cleanup, WAL/checkpoint maintenance, and external-copy obligations separately.

V3-36.09.title: Already delivered context and recipient-controlled copies are outside local purge control and are reported clearly with a fresh-conversation recommendation.

V3-36.10.title: Deletion requests by a subject (not owner) about social memory or perspective claims are honored within the same authority domain through a review workflow with audit.

V3-37.01.title: The default store is plaintext SQLite with documented filesystem-encryption guidance; an optional encrypted engine uses reviewed page-level authenticated encryption covering database, WAL, and backups [S86, S87, S88].

V3-37.02.title: Keys are acquired through the bound host's keyring or an explicit provider; keys never appear in configuration files, logs, exports, or status output.

V3-37.03.title: Vault scope wrapping keys and per-entry data keys are separate from optional whole-store encryption keys; ordinary sanitized indexes have no invented index key. Rotating a wrapping key rewraps covered data keys with checkpoints, while rotating a data key re-encrypts the covered value. Recovery and backup dependencies follow §35.12.

V3-37.04.title: An encrypted store never falls back to plaintext silently; unavailable keys produce a `locked` health state.

V3-37.05.title: Backups use snapshot mechanisms consistent with the engine, include schema and erasure ledger coverage, and exclude secrets.

V3-37.06.title: Restore defaults to a fresh inactive destination, validates integrity, reapplies erasure knowledge, and requires explicit activation.

V3-37.07.title: Recovery drills cover corrupted indexes, missing optional models, interrupted writes, lost keys, pre-erasure backups, and partially applied migrations.

V3-37.08.title: Neither whole-store encryption nor per-entry keys alone establish selective cryptographic erasure. Claims require §35.05's key-copy destruction/revocation evidence. Restoring a ciphertext/key-wrap backup with an available wrapping key must demonstrate why the reference provider reports logical deletion rather than an unsupported cryptographic guarantee.

V3-37.09.title: Encryption overhead (CPU, latency, storage) is measured and published per profile before the feature is recommended.

V3-37.10.title: Power-loss guarantees are stated within engine/filesystem/hardware limits; unsupported network filesystems are rejected for writable production stores.

V3-38.01.title: A `StorageEngine` interface defines transactions, repositories, index generations, capability reports (FTS, vectors, sparse, late interaction, encryption), backup, integrity checks, and maintenance; both engines pass one semantics conformance suite.

V3-38.02.title: SQLite remains the authority for embedded and local profiles; a server engine is introduced only after the conformance suite and §44 mixed-load matrix pass on it.

V3-38.03.title: SQL is parameterized over fixed column allowlists; no ORM, dynamic identifiers, or string-built predicates.

V3-38.04.title: Connections are thread-owned or explicitly synchronized; busy waits are bounded by the smaller of the contention timeout and the remaining request deadline.

V3-38.05.title: Store creation validates the approved root, ownership, permissions, and symlink behavior; read-only, disk-full, I/O, and corrupt-store failures cannot return a durable success receipt.

V3-38.06.title: Blob artifacts are content-addressed, size-capped per kind, quota-limited per scope, and purge-aware; blob references never leak filesystem paths to callers.

V3-38.07.title: Engine capability reports drive `status`; an engine lacking a capability disables dependent lanes visibly.

V3-38.08.title: Migrations require an application-level exclusive maintenance lease, compatible-client checks, preflight (space, backup, keys, digest, active clients), and resumable checkpoints.

V3-39.01.title: Migrations are additive and ordered; rebuilds that widen CHECK constraints run as separate fenced transactions with foreign-key verification (v2 jobs rebuild precedent).

V3-39.02.title: Every table carries a scope or a derivation path to a scoped object so purge closure and authorization partitioning are total.

V3-39.03.title: JSON columns are validated against versioned schemas on write; identifiers, revisions, epochs, and sequences are typed columns, never JSON.

V3-39.04.title: Foreign keys are enforced on every connection; enumerations use CHECK constraints or lookup tables with migration coverage.

V3-39.05.title: The schema digest covers all DDL including index tables; an unexpected digest blocks writes with an explicit upgrade path.

V3-39.06.title: Sequence numbers (`content_seq`), policy, authorization, erasure epochs, and index generations remain distinct counters.

V3-39.07.title: `derivations` supports forward (impact), reverse (provenance), and time-bounded traversal with bounded fan-out and cycle protection.

V3-40.01.title: The v2 job contract remains: durable obligations, stable operation keys, lease generations, commit fencing, receipts committed with effects, and redelivery replaying receipts.

V3-40.02.title: Compilation pipelines are chains of idempotent jobs with checkpoints; a crash between stages resumes without duplicating episodes, transitions, or procedures.

V3-40.03.title: Background pipelines yield to foreground recall and privacy operations through budgets and cancellation points; a saturated background lane never blocks privacy work.

V3-40.04.title: Model-assisted stages run outside write transactions and recheck input revisions, leases, permissions, epochs, and taint before committing.

V3-40.05.title: Queue limits are per lane; exceeding ordinary limits applies backpressure to hosts through receipts, never silent drops.

V3-40.06.title: Every job records stage latency, retries, and outcome for observability; job payloads never contain evidence text beyond identifiers.

V3-40.07.title: A worker with an expired or replaced lease cannot commit domain effects even after receiving a valid model response.

V3-41.01.title: Index generations exist per kind (lexical, dense, sparse, late interaction, procedural signature); each generation has a manifest, snapshot sequence, coverage verification, and atomic pointer swap.

V3-41.02.title: Incremental admission and transitions update the active generation transactionally; rebuilds catch up through an outbox and swap only when complete.

V3-41.03.title: Encoder identity includes backend, artifact digest, tokenizer, pooling, dimensions, dtype, normalization, and preprocessing versions; mixed generations are never compared.

V3-41.04.title: Matryoshka-style encoders MAY store full vectors and prefilter with truncated prefixes followed by exact full-dimension rescoring; the truncation policy is part of the manifest [S71].

V3-41.05.title: Quantized and compressed vectors are separately versioned and evaluated; source evidence is unchanged.

V3-41.06.title: Multilingual encoder and reranker candidates are research inputs selected through held-out retrieval quality, latency, license, and platform gates; no automatic download or default selection occurs.

V3-41.07.title: Artifact provisioning is an explicit operator action recording digest, license, runtime versions, resource estimate, and label mapping; loaders never fetch missing files or execute repository code.

V3-41.08.title: ANN structures remain research until filter-correctness, recall loss, deletion propagation, rebuild, and resource tests pass; exact search remains the recoverable reference path.

V3-41.09.title: Missing or stale vectors leave lexical evidence available with explicit coverage and lag indicators.

V3-41.10.title: Resident memory, disk, and rebuild time per index kind are published per profile; a 100000 by 1024 float32 matrix alone is 409.6 MB before overhead and MUST be accounted separately from runtime memory.

V3-42.01.title: Requests include immutable input references, digests, exact allowed outputs, task/rubric version, scope, epochs, deadline, and purpose; results include backend identity, typed outcome, calibrated score if any, abstention reason, usage, and latency.

V3-42.02.title: Rules are the default for every task; local non-generative classifiers and cross-encoders are the first model option; generative judges remain outside the approved zero-generation path unless a separately named opt-in design is approved.

V3-42.03.title: A backend advertises only tasks and languages it supports and abstains otherwise; no task routes silently to a generative fallback.

V3-42.04.title: Calibration is per task, artifact, rubric, language, domain, and action; automation eligibility requires the G2/G3/G5 gates and prospective drift monitoring.

V3-42.05.title: Jev and Cloudflare transports keep their v2 contracts; remote decisions require consent, budget, and sanitized inputs, and never receive vault values.

V3-42.06.title: Decisions are cached by ordered context, artifact, rubric, task, scope, and epochs; artifact changes invalidate caches and automation eligibility.

V3-42.07.title: Parse failures, schema drift, timeouts, and unsupported domains produce abstention or review, never a guessed positive.

V3-42.08.title: `OUTCOME_CLASS` cannot upgrade an outcome beyond what a checker artifact supports; text claiming success without an artifact yields `unknown`.

V3-43.10.title: Feedback labels record actor authority, target revision, context, and explicit/inferred status; utility votes are never correctness labels.

V3-44.01.title: Reference measurement uses the inherited four-core, 16 GiB RAM, local-SSD CPU envelope, one writer and four recall clients, with actual CPU/OS/runtime pinned in the manifest. Warm measurements include query encoding, policy checks, screening, packing, serialization, and final authorization; cold model load is reported separately. T1/T2 rules targets above and a T2 local-semantic p95 target of 200 ms are v3.0 gates; T3/T4 are optional scale claims. Workload distributions include revisions, dependencies, procedures, and security metadata, and targets are not promises for every machine.

V3-44.02.title: Scale claims require measured envelopes at the claimed tier including ingestion throughput, compilation lag, index rebuild time, purge closure time, and mixed-load behavior.

V3-44.03.title: Maintenance has CPU, I/O, memory, concurrency, and cancellation budgets and yields to foreground recall and privacy operations.

V3-44.04.title: Derived-object growth is bounded per scope; consolidation and retention reviews trigger before soft limits, and evidence is never evicted automatically.

V3-44.05.title: Capacity planning counts evidence, derived objects, vectors, sparse/late indexes, blobs, WAL, backups, replay artifacts, and temporary rebuild space separately.

V3-44.06.title: Readers use short snapshots; encoding, compilation, and inference operate outside them to avoid pinning WAL indefinitely.

V3-44.07.title: Idle maintenance runs only while an engine or explicit worker is running; no cron, service, or respawn loop is installed.

V3-44.08.title: Connection and worker pools are keyed by immutable database/profile identity with process-wide caps for many-profile hosts.

V3-44.09.title: Bounded scans report incomplete coverage when deadlines prevent full search; exact-search claims apply only to completed eligible-corpus scans.

V3-45.01.title: Memory operations emit structured events (create, read, update, delete, share, hydrate, quarantine, purge) with identity, provenance, epoch, and safe identifiers; events never carry evidence text by default.

V3-45.02.title: Spans and metrics align with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions for retrieval and memory operations where they exist, with Verbatim-specific attributes namespaced [S79].

V3-45.03.title: Metrics cover accepted sources, stage lag, admission/review fractions, quarantine rate, conflict coverage, index lag per kind, controller route distribution, abstention rate, tokens per pack, negative-transfer signals, purge stages, vault hydrations, and remote spend.

V3-45.04.title: Influence and blast-radius queries are first-class observability surfaces (§32).

V3-45.05.title: Logs omit raw source/query text, credentials, private paths, and provider bodies; content debugging requires explicit temporary authorization with bounded retention and purge tracking.

V3-45.06.title: Metadata-only diagnostic export to SIEM-style sinks is an explicit operator action, never default telemetry.

V3-45.07.title: High-cardinality per-query metrics and unbounded event payloads cannot become an accidental second memory store.

V3-46.01.title: Errors contain stable code, safe message, retryable flag, and optional scoped detail handle; raw provider exceptions are never public output.

V3-46.02.title: Health states are `ready`, `degraded`, `read_only`, `backpressured`, `locked`, `quarantine_backlog`, and `unavailable`, each with per-capability reasons.

V3-46.03.title: Unknown internal failures never become successful empty results; safe local fallback is reserved for classified optional-capability failures.

V3-46.04.title: CLI exit classes remain 0 success, 2 usage/config, 3 unavailable capability, 4 authorization, 5 retryable, 6 integrity; partial outcomes are explicit JSON data.

V3-46.05.title: Status distinguishes configured, functioning, measured, and recommended capabilities and reports effective mode, profile, and policy revisions.

V3-46.06.title: Error detail handles are scoped to the caller and expire; dereferencing a handle reauthorizes the underlying objects and never reveals identifiers from other scopes.

V3-46.07.title: Health transitions (for example `ready` to `quarantine_backlog`) are emitted as observability events with reasons so hosts can surface degraded memory to operators without reading logs.

V3-47.01.title: Public requests and results are immutable typed snapshots with `wire_version: 3`; inputs are recursively copied and validated before asynchronous use, and mutable repository rows never escape.

V3-47.02.title: Every request validates types, bounds, verbs, purpose, and object scope before dereferencing private identifiers.

V3-47.03.title: Mutation responses include operation id, committed event sequence, affected revisions, outstanding asynchronous stages, and any quarantine or review created.

V3-47.04.title: Cancellation before commit returns no committed effect; cancellation after commit exposes the receipt recoverably.

V3-47.05.title: Library users supply clocks and fake capabilities for deterministic tests; production factories enforce the same gates as transport adapters.

V3-47.06.title: Unprivileged transports receive opaque audience-bound snapshot/cursor tokens; trusted diagnostics may use numeric sequences with reauthorization on translation.

V3-47.07.title: v2 calls remain supported through adapters where semantics are representable; unrepresentable requests fail with a version/capability error rather than flattening perspectives, taint, or freshness away.

V3-47.08.title: The Python package is the reference implementation; a TypeScript client speaks the HTTP/MCP surface and contains no admission, authorization, or storage logic.

V3-47.09.title: No administrative operation is reachable through model-visible tools; `admin` and `review` operations require operator surfaces.

V3-48.01.title: The stdio MCP server remains the zero-code integration: process launch binds profile, caller identity, verbs, purposes, and approved root; credentials come from the environment per MCP guidance, and no OAuth flow runs over stdio [S74].

V3-48.02.title: The optional HTTP MCP server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server: it publishes Protected Resource Metadata, validates token audience, requires PKCE-capable authorization servers, never passes tokens through to upstreams, and maps scopes to verbs and purposes [S74, S75].

V3-48.03.title: Fine-grained authorization MAY use `authorization_details` (RFC 9396) to express scope, verbs, and purpose in one grant; absent it, scope strings map to a published verb table [S76].

V3-48.04.title: Model-visible tools are `verbatim_capture`, `verbatim_recall`, `verbatim_evidence`, `verbatim_remember`, `verbatim_feedback`, and `verbatim_procedure`; capture follows §13's agent-note/host-handle distinction. Names and schemas remain stable within a session, and revoked permissions deny calls without changing the tool list. Startup capabilities expose whether explicit capture is authorized; a disabled capture tool cannot infer consent from its invocation.

V3-48.05.title: Tool arguments cannot select profiles, actors, endpoints, grants, approvals, or purposes beyond those bound at launch; such arguments are rejected.

V3-48.06.title: Resources and detail handles are authorized at read time and never expose filesystem paths or executable templates.

V3-48.07.title: Requests are bounded to 1 MiB, eight in-flight per client, and engine hard budgets; cancellation propagates to bounded work.

V3-48.08.title: MCP elicitation MAY present consent/review requests when supported [S73], but decisions are accepted only from an authenticated human operator flow bound to the exact request/effect digest and expected versions. Model tool arguments or an untrusted client response cannot mint operator authority. Core recall never waits indefinitely for elicitation; unavailable approval leaves the action denied/pending.

V3-48.09.title: The engine does not depend on MCP sampling; an observed draft revision marks sampling deprecated, and no Verbatim feature requires server-initiated model calls [S77].

V3-48.10.title: Long-running operations (investigate, replay, purge) MAY expose progress through MCP task mechanisms where supported and otherwise through receipts and `wait_ready`.

V3-48.11.title: The A2A adapter publishes a memory-handoff extension on the agent card; capsules travel as typed artifacts with offline-verifiable capability tokens, and no A2A message carries raw scopes or grants [S72].

V3-48.12.title: The optional ACP adapter translates editor-agent events at depth 1 only under a separately issued capture authorization (§11.11). ACP permission results prove approval of the named tool operation, not consent to durable retention of its input/output [S78]. Missing capture consent discards content before persistence even when the tool was permitted; capture policy, scope, and expiry are checked independently on every event.

V3-48.13.title: Remote exposure requires TLS, origin/host validation, body and rate limits, and an explicit deployment review; no public binding is a default.

V3-49.01.title: Adapters translate only; each documents its capability matrix (capture kinds, hooks, outcome delivery, compaction archive, identity binding) and passes the conformance kit.

V3-49.02.title: Framework-provided JSON memories are `imported` external-app records with stated provenance, never authenticated user testimony.

V3-49.03.title: Hermes remains a thin out-of-tree plugin using the tested provider contract; per-turn author identity, `spawn_context_thread`, byte-stable system guidance, and A→B→A isolation tests remain mandatory.

V3-49.04.title: Adapters expose no verb the launching principal lacks and add no storage, admission, or screening logic of their own.

V3-49.05.title: Session/history stores (OpenAI Sessions, Microsoft history providers) are treated as transcripts; memory derivation from them requires capture permission and passes the same ladder.

V3-49.06.title: Each adapter ships integration tests against a pinned host revision with two temporary homes and fresh-session recall.

V3-50.01.title: File projection renders authorized memory as Markdown with YAML frontmatter (object ids, revisions, provenance, perspective, taint, freshness, derived/exact marker) plus wikilinks mapped to entity and claim identifiers; it is a view, never the canonical store.

V3-50.02.title: Projection is read-only by default; when writable, edits become operator records on explicit re-import with diff receipts, and a conflicting concurrent engine change produces a review rather than a silent overwrite.

V3-50.03.title: Projection excludes vault values, quarantined items, and other-perspective content by default; sensitive placeholders render as placeholders.

V3-50.04.title: Bundles use a versioned manifest, bounded JSONL records, optional assets and vectors, portable digests, license and provenance references, and capability tokens; default exports exclude secrets, keys, model weights, caches, outbound bodies, suppressed evidence, and vault values.

Report both, net success difference, and uncertainty rather than asserting individual causal attribution from an influence handle. Unnecessary disclosure means delivering a task-unneeded sensitive value even to an otherwise authorized recipient; unauthorized disclosure is a separate zero-tolerance G1 violation.

Insufficient sample support is `inconclusive`, not passed. Report sensitivity-detector misses separately from value-routing violations.

Gateway conformance and ungated host-model resistance are different tracks.

V3-57.01.title: Migration never runs implicitly; opening a v2 store reports the explicit upgrade path and remains read-only until the operator runs `migrate` with preflight and a backup.

V3-57.02.title: Schema changes are additive: new tables from §39, extended `procedures` columns with defaults, and index-generation kinds; existing identifiers, bytes, offsets, events, and receipts are preserved except for separately approved privacy transformations/purge under §57.06.
