V3-57.03.title: Perspectives are backfilled from existing scope ownership and per-turn authorship where recorded; unknown roles are stored as `unknown`, never guessed.

V3-57.04.title: Backfill provenance from verified legacy host bindings, not source-kind strings alone. Attested user messages may remain `principal_direct`, tool transports `host_observed`, and imports `imported`; unknown authors stay unknown. Initialize content form/risk as `unknown`/`unassessed` until screening, with an explicit report and no blanket `clean` assignment. Preserved legacy evidence may remain in its original authorized archive lane, but new promotion, sharing, or action-ticket eligibility requires current checks.

V3-57.05.title: Existing procedures migrate to `candidate` unless previously approved, in which case they remain `active` with an `unrefined` marker and no failure evidence claim.

V3-57.06.title: A sensitivity scan proposes vault migration for S2/S3 matches and purge candidates for S4 matches; nothing is rewritten without operator approval, and quotations remain honest through redaction spans.

V3-57.07.title: The controller starts in deterministic mode; observations, learned policies, automatic promotion, and balanced admission remain disabled after migration.

V3-57.08.title: Configuration migrates from version 2 to 3 with dry-run impact counts; unknown or contradictory v2 keys fail migration with guidance.

V3-57.09.title: Lexical projections are rebuilt into a complete generation, including n-gram projections for unsegmented scripts, without admitting pending claims.

V3-57.10.title: Rollback uses the preserved v2 snapshot and a fresh session; post-migration writes require an explicit export strategy rather than a promised lossless downgrade.

V3-57.11.title: Migration ships with regression runs of A01–A25 on migrated stores and reports any behavior change from F24 abstention calibration.

V3-58.01.title: Each phase starts only after user authorization to build; this document is not that authorization.

V3-58.02.title: Ownership areas are storage/engines, governance/privacy, evidence/harvest, experience producers, retrieval/controller, security/screening, adapters/interfaces, and evaluation; shared contracts freeze before parallel work.

V3-58.03.title: Parallel workers own disjoint files; integration owners wire cross-area contracts with consumer tests in the same change; a unit-green leaf module is not integrated.

V3-58.04.title: A failed optional gate keeps the capability disabled or experimental; a failed core integrity, privacy, or security gate blocks release.

V3-58.05.title: Scratch profiles and synthetic data are used until separate owner approval for a canary; a live provider is never switched silently.

V3-58.06.title: Each phase closes with a registry/test/result ledger and a limitations list, not only file or test counts.

V3-58.07.title: Research subsystems that fail to beat simpler baselines are removed from the recommended profile and documented as negative results.

V3-58.08.title: Every slice adds authorization, dependency invalidation, purge, restart, and resource tests with the feature; P6 extends them under fault/mixed-load conditions rather than introducing privacy for the first time. Shared prerequisites can be built earlier, but phase exit cannot depend on an undeclared later capability.

V3-58.09.title: Evaluation runs continuously from P0. Fixture-driven conformance uses local fake model boundaries; empirical G4/G5/G9 runs require separately authorized model artifacts or synthetic-data inference budgets. Missing permission, licensing, or statistically sufficient runs leaves the gate pending, never replaced by mock success.

V3-59.01.title: The Python core deliberately adds the required reviewed `cryptography` dependency for authenticated vault encryption; this replaces the v2 zero-required-dependency packaging choice, not its offline/no-generation contract. Pin the reviewed version and wheels at implementation/release lock time under the existing dependency-age policy; do not install anything during specification work. Keyring integration and whole-store encryption are separate capabilities. Adapter/model/service extras remain explicit: `mcp`, `http`, `semantic`, `sparse`, `late`, `encrypt`, `adapters-adk`, `adapters-autogen`, `adapters-msaf`, `adapters-openai`, `adapters-langgraph`, `adapters-crewai`, `adapters-pydantic`, `a2a`, `acp`, `workbench`, `eval`.

V3-59.02.title: The TypeScript client is a separate package with no engine logic; the capture SDK schema is published as versioned JSON Schema.

V3-59.03.title: Supported Python (≥ 3.11), SQLite, and OS matrices come from native CI; FTS5 and encryption capabilities are checked at runtime and reported.

V3-59.04.title: Release artifacts ship with SBOM (SPDX), in-toto attestations, signed digests, reproducible locks, third-party notices, migration notes, and tested host revisions [S90].

V3-59.05.title: Dependencies use bounded compatible ranges and prefer releases at least seven days old; exceptions require review, never relaxed repository security controls.

V3-59.06.title: Model artifacts are provisioned by immutable digest with license manifests and explicit operator intent; datasets are never bundled without verified redistribution rights.

V3-59.07.title: Release builds contain no private transcripts, account identifiers, tokens, developer stores, or provider request bodies.

V3-59.08.title: Documentation covers quickstart per integration depth, profiles, evidence fidelity, governance, privacy limits, poisoning defenses, correction/purge, recovery, benchmarks, and known limitations.

V3-59.09.title: Security reporting and dependency update procedures are documented before public release; no certification is claimed without assessment.

V3-59.10.title: Deprecations state replacement, migration behavior, and support window; silently changing temporal, privacy, taint, or freshness semantics is a breaking change.

V3-60.01.title: Product owner approves behavior and defaults; security owner approves trust boundaries; evaluation owner freezes metrics and splits; maintainers select reviewed artifacts; one person holding all roles still records separate decisions.

V3-60.02.title: More memory kinds increase capability and maintenance; more lanes increase recall and latency; stronger screening increases safety and false positives; every default above records its accepted cost.

V3-60.03.title: No design infers objective truth from equally plausible conflicting sources; unresolved output remains a correct result.

V3-60.04.title: Unresolved evidence includes the real-world effect of learned routing, the transfer rate of compiled procedures across hosts, encoder choices for unsegmented scripts, and server-engine scaling; each has a declared experiment in §53.

V3-60.05.title: Hiding these costs to claim no downsides would contradict the evidence-first promise.

V3-60.06.title: Each decision D13–D26 has a named owner, a review date tied to the next evaluation cycle, and a rollback path; reversing a decision after activation requires a migration note and dry-run impact counts.

V3-61.01.title: Repository metadata and documentation pages are not performance measurements, security audits, or complete license reviews.

V3-61.02.title: No competitor stack, model bake-off, or comparative Verbatim benchmark was executed while writing this specification.

V3-61.03.title: Dated sources and pinned manifests are preserved before publishing claims; mutable documentation is never treated as an immutable benchmark artifact.

V3-62.02.title: Every implementation change links requirement identifiers, entry points, marked tests, migration effects, and rollout implications.

V3-62.03.title: Enum additions in `core/types.py`, schema validators, and API validators change together; no layer accepts a value another rejects.

V3-62.04.title: Adapters and compatibility layers cannot bypass taint, perspective, freshness, or vault semantics; unrepresentable requests return a clear version/capability error.

V3-62.05.title: Implementation status is reported per capability and gate through the complete-evidence registry, never inferred from this document's completeness.
